name: Iberian conifer forests
about: The pine and juniper sierras of Spain: dense black pine over the pale limestone rims and gorges of the Serranía de Cuenca, the Alto Tajo and the Cazorla and Segura sierras, Scots pine on the granite Guadarrama and the high Montes Universales, maritime pine on the red sandstone of Albarracín, Spanish juniper woodland and straw-coloured pastures with creeping juniper on the high plateaus of the Universales and the Maestrazgo, and the bare, tawny schist of the Sierra Nevada above its pine plantations; between the sierras lie cereal páramos with holm and Portuguese oak, and stone or whitewashed villages under low tile roofs. No split: the pieces are separate mountain blocks with one continental Mediterranean climate, so one haze, weather and grade fit all of them; the bare crests of the Sierra Nevada and the Guadarrama take the barren rule and the snowline, the belts from holm oak and Aleppo pine through black and Scots pine to creeping juniper and broom take the tree elevation bands, the summer-straw pastures and the farmland of the Alcarria take Sentinel-2 colour and the seasonal ramps, limestone, granite, sandstone and schist take their rock colour by lithology, and the white Andalusian villages take the house style by subdivision.
